title: SOD1 co-pathologies in the brain: insights from neuropathological evidence and implications
title_zh: SOD1在大脑中的共病：来自病理学证据的洞察与意义
abstract: Abstract Superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1), originally regarded as an antioxidant enzyme, is now recognized as a multifunctional protein whose conformational instability and aggregation contribute to neurodegeneration. The emerging evidence suggests that SOD1 pathology extends beyond amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, supporting a role in multiple neurodegenerative diseases. This review summarizes current neuropathological evidence of SOD1 co-pathologies in the human brain, with particular emphasis on its associations with TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43), tau, alpha-synuclein, amyloid-β, and other aggregation-prone proteins. We examine the distribution of pathological SOD1 species across neurodegenerative diseases, their coexistence in affected brain regions, and potential mechanisms underlying these interactions, including oxidative stress, impaired proteostasis, aberrant phase separation, and cross-seeding. We also discuss emerging observations of SOD1 pathology in neurological conditions beyond classical neurodegenerative diseases, raising the possibility that SOD1 misfolding represents a broader cellular response to neuronal injury. Collectively, the available evidence supports a shift from viewing SOD1 as a disease-specific protein to considering it a potential participant in interconnected proteopathic networks. Although the functional significance of SOD1 co-pathologies remains incompletely understood, elucidating the molecular basis of aggregation may provide new insights into disease onset and progression, improving our understanding of neurodegenerative mechanisms, and facilitating the development of biomarkers and the identification of therapeutic targets across diverse proteinopathies.
abstract_zh: 摘要 超氧化物歧化酶1（SOD1）最初被视为抗氧化酶，现已被认定为一种多功能蛋白，其构象不稳定性和聚集导致神经退行性变。新兴证据表明，SOD1病理不仅限于肌萎缩侧索硬化症，提示其在多种神经退行性疾病中发挥作用。本文综述了人类大脑中SOD1共病的最新病理学证据，重点讨论其与TAR DNA结合蛋白43（TDP‑43）、tau、α‑突触核蛋白、淀粉样β以及其他易聚集蛋白的关联。我们考察了不同神经退行性疾病中病理性SOD1物种的分布、它们在受影响脑区的共存情况，以及潜在的相互作用机制，包括氧化应激、蛋白稳态受损、异常相分离和交叉诱导。还讨论了SOD1病理在传统神经退行性疾病之外的神经疾病中的新观察，提出SOD1错误折叠可能是对神经元损伤的更广泛细胞反应。总体而言，现有证据支持从将SOD1视为疾病特异性蛋白转变为考虑其为互联蛋白病网络的潜在参与者。尽管SOD1共病的功能意义尚未完全阐明，阐明其聚集的分子基础可能为疾病发病和进展提供新见解，提升我们对神经退行性机制的理解，并促进跨多种蛋白病的生物标志物开发和治疗靶点识别。
